regime_context: The detector shows a strongly bifurcated theme tape: Memory/HBM & Storage is the clean #1 with a huge score gap over #2 Non-AI Software (2.36 vs 1.28), but breadth of rotation is narrow (23/49 eligible, 'narrowing') and momentum rank-IC is effectively nil — this is an attention map, not a return forecast. The only validated leg is the absolute-trend gate (gate_helps=true), so themes flagged eligible/trend get a drawdown-control nod, not an alpha nod. Track record shows decent hit rate (0.611) but poor directional accuracy (0.444), so default conviction low.
emerging_watch: Watching a potential confirmed handoff away from the crowded Software/Cybersecurity cluster toward uncrowded trend themes: if Non-AI Software (IGV) or Cybersecurity (CIBR) prints two consecutive weeks of negative absolute returns while US Energy Complex (XLE) or uncrowded equal-weight energy holds its 10-week trend, that would retire the 'crowded software still leads' read and signal a leadership shift worth a deeper look.

theses.subject: Non-AI Software
theses.thesis: Despite rank #2 and trend eligibility, Non-AI Software carries the most concerning crowding texture in the high-rank set: crowding_z 1.39 with 'crowded' flag true, durability_bar high-ish (0.75) but breadth extreme (0.857). Sole overweight-eligible themes should prefer durability without a crowding flag per the guardrail that crowding is a size-down caution, not a fade. The underweight lean reflects avoiding adding exposure to a crowded leader-lagging theme rather than predicting reversal.
evidence: crowding_z 1.39, crowded=true (highest-z among scorable top ranks)
breadth 0.857 — very broad participation but concentrates flow
trend-gate eligible (validated leg for drawdown control, but no return edge)
theses.dissent: Broad durability (0.75) with high breadth means the theme is fundamentally strong and still in a trend; crowding on a well-diversified software basket may persist for months without a drawdown, and underweighting gives up participation in continued leadership.

falsifier.text: IGV outperforms the S&P 500 by more than 3% over the next ~42 trading days despite the crowding flag

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: Ranked #5, trend-eligible, but crowding_z 1.51 is the highest in the entire eligible set and 'crowded' flag is true. Durability is moderate (0.75) and breadth decent (0.6). Under the guardrail that crowding is a size-down caution, this theme warrants a lean underweight relative to uncrowded trend candidates — not a short, just reduced favor.
theses.dissent: Cybersecurity has a structural demand narrative (rising breach frequency, regulation) that can sustain a crowded trade longer than a momentum-driven theme; high crowding may simply reflect justified positioning in a durable secular grower.

falsifier.text: CIBR holds up or rises while the broad market corrects, showing crowding is not a drawdown risk in practice

theses.subject: US Energy Complex
theses.thesis: Rank #3, trend-gate eligible, and a healthy durability_bar (0.68) with strong breadth (0.818). Crowding_z 1.0 is elevated/true but not extreme, and energy is a top-3 theme with a mixed hurst tag that still passes the validated absolute-trend gate. The lean overweight is justified by eligibility + relative durability in a narrow tape rather than any momentum-alpha claim. Pair against the equal-weight Energy theme which carries lower crowding (0.49) — the cap-weighted complex is the scorable proxy (XLE).
evidence: hurts_tag mixed but absolute-trend gate validated for this market
crowding_z 1.0, crowded=true (size-down caution, not a fade)
theses.dissent: Crowding is elevated and energy is a cyclical/value complex vulnerable to a growth scare or geopolitical de-escalation; if macro flips to risk-off, energy can undercut the durable-trend thesis quickly.

falsifier.text: XLE breaks below its 40-day moving average or lags SPY by more than 5% before the check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
